meta.description: Knowledge graph for the ManiSkill StackCube task: a Franka Panda (7 arm joints + parallel gripper) grasps cube A (red, 2cm) and stacks it on cube B (green, 2cm) on a table. Consumed by the P4-LLM SELECTOR to ground which failed rollout is the most informative to correct next. The novice is a diffusion policy; failures are detected by the policy's OWN diffusion loss (high loss = out-of-distribution / uncertain state); the expert is a rule-based panda motion planner that re-plans grasp->lift->align->release from the divergence state. The selector picks the ONE failed candidate whose on-policy correction closes the most impactful failure mode.
meta.control_mode: pd_joint_pos (policy acts in rel_joint_pos = 7 joint deltas + 1 gripper command)

properties.role: the cube to pick up and place on cube B
the stationary base cube; cube A must rest on its top face
grasps cube A; opens to release
properties.approach_matters: must grasp cube A on opposing faces with a feasible top-down approach

properties.expert_action: panda motion planner → absolute joint qpos + gripper (recorded as the same 8-dim demo)

properties.meaning: per-step out-of-distribution / uncertainty; peak loss marks the divergence step t*

nodes.label: A stacked on B, static, released

properties.metric: cubeA xy within ~cube-half-size of cubeB AND z-offset == 2*half_size AND cubeA static AND gripper not grasping

properties.description: Gripper closes without securing cube A (off-center approach, fingers slip, or never reaches the cube).
Cube A is grasped then slips/falls during lift or transport before reaching cube B.
Cube A is released off-center: xy offset from cube B exceeds tolerance, so it does not rest stably on top.
Arm/cube A collides with cube B and displaces it, destroying the target stack location.
Cube A lands on cube B but topples or keeps moving (released with momentum / unstable contact), so the static check fails.
Cube A is positioned correctly but the gripper does not open, so is_grasped stays true and success never registers.
Episode reaches the step horizon without success (hesitation, oscillation, slow approach).
close the gripper on cube A's opposing faces
raise cube A clear of the table
move cube A over cube B's top-center
open the gripper and let cube A settle statically

reasoning_implications.selection_objective: Among the top-3 FAILED candidate rollouts (highest peak diffusion loss), pick the ONE whose on-policy expert correction is the most informative demonstration — the failure that, once corrected, closes the most impactful / most frequent failure mode and most improves held-out success.
reasoning_implications.missed_grasp: Earliest-phase failure (reach/grasp). Correcting it teaches reliable grasping, which is a prerequisite for ALL later phases — usually the highest-leverage correction when grasping is the bottleneck.
reasoning_implications.dropped_in_transit: Grasp succeeded but transport failed. Correcting it teaches a stable lift/carry; valuable once grasping is reliable but stacking is not yet reached.
reasoning_implications.misaligned_stack: Late-phase failure: the policy reaches cube B but places off-center. Correcting it teaches fine alignment over cube B's top-center — high value when the policy already grasps and transports.
reasoning_implications.not_static: Release timing/stability failure. Correcting it teaches a gentle release so cube A settles — valuable when placements are close but unstable.
reasoning_implications.no_release: Trivial-to-fix end-phase failure (gripper never opens). Lower priority unless it is the dominant failure mode.
reasoning_implications.knocked_base: Collision that destroys the target; correcting it teaches collision-free approach to cube B.
reasoning_implications.diversity: Prefer a failure whose phase/mode is NOT already well-covered by recent corrections, so each added demonstration expands coverage rather than repeating an already-learned skill.
reasoning_implications.peak_loss_tiebreak: If two candidates target the same failure mode, prefer the higher peak diffusion loss (more out-of-distribution) and the one whose divergence is earlier (more downstream behaviour to teach).
reasoning_implications.workspace_constraint: Both cubes spawn flat on the table within x[-0.10,0.10] y[-0.20,0.20] z=0.02 (cube half-size 0.02), with random z-rotation and a collision-avoidance gap between them; the gripper TCP operates within x[-0.35,0.35] y[-0.35,0.35] z[0.02,0.30]. Any prescribed config (for the p4_top3 prescription arm) MUST keep cubeA/cubeB and the TCP inside these ranges, or the expert cannot solve it and the round is wasted.
reasoning_implications.non_emptiness: A failure is present, so any prescription MUST be a concrete, fully-specified, in-bounds config (non-empty cubeA_xyz, cubeB_xyz). Never emit an empty prescription.
